candidates.title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces
candidates.abstract: Abstract Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular model, steering generated molecules toward two large make-on-demand spaces: Enamine REAL and Freedom 4.0. We compare an offline, preference-based strategy (direct preference optimization, DPO) and an online RL strategy (DiffusionNFT) across single-target and multi-target settings. In single-target optimization for KRAS, the fraction of unique purchasable candidates rises from 10.0% to 25.5% for Enamine REAL and from 4.3% to 12.1% for Freedom 4.0, while drug-likeness and docking-based affinity proxies are preserved. In multi-target optimization, DPO achieves consistent improvements across diverse protein targets, including a 23-fold increase for the challenging CDK4 pocket. These results demonstrate that RL alignment can substantially improve the experimental accessibility of SBDD candidates without sacrificing structural or chemical quality.

candidates.title: Optimal-transport flow matching for stochastic model ipdating
candidates.abstract: Deep generative models have attracted considerable attention as inference engines for stochastic model updating. Among these deep generative models, conditional flow matching offers a particularly efficient formulation, in which a continuous transport map from a latent distribution to the posterior is learned by regression against optimal-transport probability paths, avoiding both the invertibility constraints of normalising flows and the iterative denoising of diffusion models. However, its performance in engineering model updating has not been examined against an established baseline such as the Bayesian updating framework under controlled conditions. In this work, conditional flow matching is therefore assessed against the Bayesian model updating approach with transitional Markov chain Monte Carlo, in which the Bhattacharyya distance provides the approximate likelihood for the Bayesian approach. The two methods are assessed with respect to posterior fidelity, evaluated by statistical distances against the known ground truth and computational expenditure in model evaluations, with the offline training budget reported separately from the inference cost of each subsequent conditioning. A 3-DOF spring–mass system with uncertain stiffness parameters serves as the benchmark. Since the calibrated posterior constitutes the input description upon which subsequent reliability assessment depends, the accuracy and the marginal cost of the updating step both bear directly on reliability computations. In addition, the amortised nature of the learned transport map is discussed in this work, as it permits the posterior to be re-evaluated under new observations at negligible cost, which is a property of practical relevance to reliability assessment under sequentially acquired monitoring data.

candidates.title: Sequence Scanning Improves Accuracy for Antibody–Antigen and Molecular Glue Ternary Complex Cofolding
candidates.abstract: Accurately modeling biomolecular interactions is crucial for understanding biological function and can accelerate drug discovery efforts. Deep-learning-based cofolding methods such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2 can successfully predict many different biomolecular complexes. However, these models show lower success rates in predicting antibody-antigen and molecular glue (MG) ternary complexes, two cases of high relevance to pharmaceutical research. Here, we present sequence scanning, a new workflow, evaluated on Boltz and Protenix, that improves prediction accuracy in these domains by applying systematic constraints to enhance overall sampling diversity. For both use cases, we assess the performance of the method on large, diverse benchmark sets. We find improved accuracy of the sequence scanning workflow in predicting antibody-antigen interface contacts and in pose prediction quality for MGs compared to previously published results. We also discuss remaining challenges and potential improvements to the method.

candidates.title: PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery
candidates.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent an emerging therapeutic modality that harnesses the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation (TPD). Their event-driven and catalytic mechanisms provide new opportunities to target previously undruggable proteins. However, the rapid expansion of TPD technologies, including molecular glues (MGs) and X-functional targeting chimeras (XTACs), together with the increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in degrader design, highlights the need for comprehensive and continuously updated data resources. Here, we present PROTAC-DB 4.0, an expanded knowledgebase covering major targeted degradation and induced-proximity technologies. Compared with the previous version, PROTAC-DB 4.0 contains 15 502 PROTAC entries, together with 24 798 MG entries and 272 XTAC entries, with expanded experimental annotations, patent-derived compounds, and modality-specific data fields. A major advancement in PROTAC-DB 4.0 is the integration of a large language model and retrieval-augmented generation-based natural language query system, which connects structured database records with scientific literature to enable intuitive knowledge discovery across PROTACs, MGs, and XTACs. By combining comprehensive data curation with AI-assisted information retrieval, PROTAC-DB 4.0 provides an accessible platform to support degrader discovery, data-driven modeling, and rational design of next-generation targeted degradation and induced-proximity therapeutics. PROTAC-DB 4.0 is freely accessible at http://cadd.zju.edu.cn/protacdb/.

candidates.title: MolecularCanvas: LLM-assisted Small-Molecule Drug Discovery via Structure-Guided Constraints
candidates.abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery relies on iterative molecular optimization, where chemists repeatedly modify candidate compounds to balance multiple competing properties such as efficacy, toxicity, and solubility. Recent advances in generative AI (GenAI), have shown promise in accelerating this process by automatically proposing new molecular structures or targeted modifications. However, existing GenAI-based molecular design tools remain poorly aligned with experts’ real-world workflows. Specifically, they offer limited support for specifying structure-level modification intents on molecules, provide insufficient transparency into model-generated modifications, and lack integrated support for downstream property evaluation with external computational tools. To address these challenges, we introduce MolecularCanvas, an interactive system that enables users to iteratively construct an optimization context by integrating high-level goals, structure-level annotations, property constraints, and reference-based preferences. This context guides the generation of candidate molecules across diverse molecular structures. MolecularCanvas further enhances transparency by providing evidence for AI-generated suggestions, and streamlines molecular evaluation by integrating commonly used property computational tools into a unified interface. Finally, a user study with 12 participants demonstrates the usefulness and effectiveness of MolecularCanvas in helping users optimize candidate molecules.

candidates.title: A benchmarking-informed structure-based virtual screening strategy targeting Lm-PTR1: Leveraging the Northern African natural products database.
candidates.abstract: Leishmaniasis is a neglected tropical disease (NTD) affecting millions worldwide. Current treatments have limitations, highlighting the need for new strategies for leishmaniasis drug discovery. Herein, we utilized a benchmarking-informed structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) strategy against Leishmania major folate pathway, especially via targeting pteridine reductase 1 (PTR1). Firstly, representative bioactive molecules against Lm-PTR1 were compiled. Secondly, a challenging DEKOIS 2.0 benchmark set was generated to assess the screening performance of three docking tools, FRED, AutoDock Vina, and PLANTS. Interestingly, FRED showed the best screening performance, with pROC-AUC of 0.84 and EF 1% of 12.5. Consequently, as an example, an ensemble VS of NANPDB using FRED against PTR1 was conducted. The results nominated three candidates for further investigations, namely Anastatin A, valoneic acid dilactone, and 1,6-di-O-galloyl glucose. To assess the binding stability of the candidates, four MD simulations for 500 ns including folic acid - PTR1 complex system as a reference were conducted. Consequently, MM-GBSA calculations and MD profiles confirmed the stable binding of valoneic dilactone and 1,6-di-O-galloyl glucose and ranked them superior to the reference folic acid. These results suggest the ability of both candidates to hinder the access of folic acid to the cofactor NADPH and hence modulate the catalytic function of Lm-PTR1. The identified candidates are recommended for subsequent in vitro evaluations in future investigations. Overall, this benchmarking strategy against Lm-PTR1 can be broadly applied to any accessible compound database for SBVS campaigns. The benchmark dataset for Lm-PTR1 will be made publicly accessible on www.dekois.com.

candidates.title: RAVEN: Frozen Random Graph Reservoirs with Physics-Informed Interaction Fingerprints for Protein–Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction
candidates.abstract: Abstract Predicting protein–ligand binding affinity directly from three-dimensional complex structures remains challenging because available structure–affinity data are limited, heterogeneous, and highly susceptible to similarity-driven data set bias. Most graph-learning approaches address this problem by optimizing molecular representations end-to-end against affinity labels, potentially coupling representation learning to data set-specific correlations. Here, we introduce RAVEN (Randomized Atomistic Views with Ensemble Neural Reservoirs), a different learning paradigm in which multiple independently initialized atomistic graph neural networks are used as fully frozen reservoirs of nonlinear structural representations. Rather than adapting the graph encoders to affinity labels, RAVEN samples multiple independently initialized structural views from the initialization-induced representation space and integrates them with deterministic, physics-informed interaction fingerprints. Heterogeneous neural and tree-based readers then exploit these representations, followed by validation-based nonnegative fusion. On a similarity-isolated PDBbind 2020R1 benchmark reconstructed using GEMS similarity criteria, RAVEN achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.8005 and an RMSE of 1.2346 pK units on the held-out test set, and a Pearson correlation of 0.8415 on the protected CASF-2016 subset. Ablation analyses further show that increasing the number of frozen graph views generally improves the predictive utility of the structure-only representation, whereas physics-informed tree-based readers exhibit distinct residual patterns that enhance heterogeneous model fusion. These results demonstrate that competitive protein–ligand affinity prediction does not require end-to-end optimization of every representation component and establish frozen randomized graph reservoirs as a modular strategy for combining structural diversity, physical priors, and complementary inductive biases in molecular prediction.

candidates.title: A comprehensive review of computational strategies in the rational design of biosensors based on allosteric transcription factors for pollutant detection
candidates.abstract: Allosteric transcription factor (aTF)-based biosensors are powerful analytical tools for the detection of different analytes such as environmental pollutants and are widely used in medical diagnostics and environmental monitoring. These biosensors rely on ligand-induced conformational changes in transcription factors that regulate gene expression, thereby positioning them as low-cost, sensitive and selective components in biosensor design. In recent times, computational biology and chemistry techniques such as homology modelling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free energy perturbation (FEP), enhanced sampling techniques and machine learning have been widely employed in the design and optimization of aTF-based biosensors. With these methods, the structures of proteins could be predicted, the ligand-binding pockets could be identified and characterized, the interactions therein could be analyzed and binding affinities could be predicted. Also, the conformational dynamics, allosteric and transition pathways, free energy landscapes, relative binding free energies of the ligand-aTF complexes can be predicted. Taken together, these can facilitate the engineering of aTFs with improved sensitivity and specificity. Therefore, this review highlights the individual and complementary roles of these computational techniques in the design and optimization of aTF-based biosensors and discusses the recent advances, current limitations and future directions in the design of next-generation aTF-based biosensors.

candidates.title: Few-shot regulatory sequence design with a genomic language model
candidates.abstract: A central challenge in generative biology is translating knowledge learned from natural sequences and experiments into designs with desired functions. In-context learning (ICL) is an emergent capability of large language models that allows them to adapt to new tasks from a few examples without additional training, enabling these models to become general-purpose learners. Here, we show that the genome language model, Evo 2, exhibits generative ICL in biological sequence design. Prompting with just tens of examples conditions Evo 2 to generate novel and diverse regulatory DNA sequences without any additional training. Mechanistic analysis suggests that genomic ICL may originate from induction, similar to phenomena observed in natural language. Reinforcement learning leveraging sequence-to-function models as experiment-derived rewards further strengthens ICL. We first validate this approach by generating enhancers that drive cell-type-specific gene expression in three human cell lines. Extending this approach in vivo, enhancers designed using human regulatory element data selectively label layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the mouse cortex with high specificity and stronger activity than existing enhancers. Our study provides evidence of emergent properties in genomic sequence models and introduces a promising approach for improving functional conditioning in generative biology.

candidates.title: MultiTargetDB: a comprehensive database of multitarget ligands for polypharmacology research and drug discovery
candidates.abstract: Multitarget drug discovery has gained considerable traction in recent years, particularly for the treatment of complex diseases. Despite the growing demand for dedicated, well-curated resources to advance polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery, such resources remain severely limited. Here, we present MultiTargetDB, a database of multitarget ligands integrated with comprehensive biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. At the small molecule level, MultiTargetDB integrates chemical structures (including molecular scaffolds), their drug development stages, and target information, whereas at the target level, MultiTargetDB incorporates protein domains and families, functional associations, and pathway-disease annotations. The current release contains 173 977 multitarget molecules, 6496 protein targets, and 474 749 standardized quantitative bioactivity records, complemented by 46 234 high-confidence protein functional associations, 370 pathways from the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and 2493 diseases. MultiTargetDB supports multitarget ligand retrieval, target-combination analysis, quantitative activity profiling, inspection of source-level evidence, and biological interpretation of molecule-target-pathway-disease relationships, with a natural-language query assistant facilitating flexible database exploration. The integrated quantitative, pharmacological and biological data further provide a basis for drug-repurposing exploration, computational modeling, and machine-learning applications. MultiTargetDB v1.0 is freely accessible at https://multitargetdb.inflygent.com/.

candidates.title: Wavelet Packet‐Based Diffusion Model for Ground Motion Generation With Multi‐Conditional Energy and Spectral Matching
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Temporal energy distribution strongly affects nonlinear structural response and cumulative damage. We propose a multi‐condition diffusion framework for ground‐motion synthesis that simultaneously matches temporal‐energy evolution and target response spectra. Wavelet packet decomposition is used to represent the ground‐motion signals and enables direct waveform reconstruction via orthogonal filter banks. A Transformer‐based conditional encoder with cross‐attention integrates heterogeneous conditions, including spectral ordinates, Arias intensity, temporal parameters, and Husid curves. The framework adopts the elucidating diffusion model (EDM) with second‐order Heun sampling to improve inference efficiency without sacrificing quality. Tests on the NGA‐West2 database show that explicit temporal‐energy constraints markedly improve control of energy onset and significant duration while preserving response‐spectrum agreement across repeated stochastic samples. The framework yields spectrum‐compatible ground motions with realistic energy evolution and enables conditional sample variability to be quantified through repeated stochastic sampling.

candidates.title: Protein co-scientist aided simulations of the structural and functional impact of O-GlcNAc Transferase TPR domain deletions and amino acid substitutions associated with X-Linked Intellectual Disability
candidates.abstract: O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) is an essential glycosyltransferase that regulates cellular processes through the addition of O-linked {beta}-N-acetyglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) to target proteins. Substrate recognition and protein-protein interactions are mediated by the tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) domain, yet the contributions of individual TPR repeats to structural stability and function remain poorly understood. Here, we employed an integrated computational framework combining an AI protein co-scientist, Speak to a Protein, which incorporates Boltz-2 for structure prediction and rDock for ligand binding evaluation, with external tools including AlphaFold3 for more advanced structure prediction and the HDOCK server for protein-protein docking. This framework was used to investigate how deletions of TPR domains and disease-associated amino acid substitutions within the TPR domain affect OGT structure and function. Five synthetic truncation OGT isoforms, thirteen single-TPR deletion variants, and five X-linked intellectual disability (XLID)-associated amino acid substitutions were modeled and aligned to wild-type OGT for comparison. Structural perturbations were quantified using backbone root mean square deviation (RMSD), while functional effects were assessed through docking analyses with UDP-GlcNAc, Host Cell Factor 1 (HCF1), and Tet methylcytosine dioxygenase 1 (TET1). Variation in TPR length altered global protein structure and induced long-range conformational changes within the catalytic domain despite no sequence modifications in that region. Single TPR deletions showed that individual repeats contribute unequally to structural stability, with deletions in mid-to-late TPR domains producing the largest structural disruptions. Disease-associated amino acid substitutions also generated conformational changes and reduced predicted ligand binding, consistent with known reductions in enzymatic activity in XLID. Protein-protein docking analyses demonstrated substrate-specific effects, as domain deletion and amino acid substitution variants of OGT had different interactions with TET1 and HCF1. Collectively, these findings identify the TPR domain as a regulatory domain that governs structure, ligand recognition, and protein interactions. More broadly, this work demonstrates how the integration of a protein co-scientist with protein structure modeling tools can be used to predict the structural and functional consequences of domain deletions or natural amino acid variants.

candidates.title: Editable Map-Conditioned Trajectory Generation for Human Mobility Simulation
candidates.abstract: Geospatial simulation of infrastructure interventions requires mobility generators that respond directly to edited maps, yet many data-driven generators do not expose the map as an editable condition. We formulate this task as map-conditioned autoregressive generation of human mobility: a road raster conditions a decoder that emits nominal 31.25 m mesh-cell tokens at one-minute intervals. The mesh-local vocabulary supports held-out and locally edited maps without retraining or vocabulary changes. We instantiate a ResNet-50 visual-prefix configuration and a Vision Transformer (ViT) cross-attention configuration, trained from scratch on 87,400 smartphone-derived trajectories from 874 meshes in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan; 219 meshes are held out. We evaluate map sensitivity by comparing correct-map and within-split shuffled-map generations with held-out real trajectories. On the 110-mesh test split, for the ResNet-50 configuration, correct-map generations are closer than shuffled-map generations on 60% of meshes under Hausdorff-based energy distance (p = 0.021), while DTW is directional but inconclusive (57%, p = 0.074); correlation with real density is 0.38 with the correct map versus 0.01 with shuffled maps. The ViT configuration shows weaker trajectory-level sensitivity and smaller density gains. An illustrative bridge-removal edit changes generated continuations without retraining. Together, these results support the feasibility of editable-map human-mobility simulation.

candidates.title: On reliable cost-efficient data-driven modelling of microwave passives in reduced-dimensionality domains with co-kriging
candidates.abstract: Data-driven surrogate modeling has seen a rise in attention in microwave engineering over the recent years. It has been primarily employed to expedite electromagnetic (EM)-based design procedures, e.g., parametric optimization or robust design. However, behavioral modeling of microwave components becomes problematic due to their nonlinear characteristics, often large numbers of geometry parameters, as well as broad ranges thereof. This work proposes an unconventional approach to resource-efficient and accurate modeling of microwave passive circuits. Our methodology is founded on reducing the design space dimensionality carried out via fast global sensitivity analysis, and also the incorporation of variable-resolution simulation data. The surrogate domain extends alongside the most significant directions reflecting the highest circuit response variability. The surrogate model is rendered using a mixture of densely sampled low- and sparsely allocated high-resolution EM simulation training points, which are blended together using co-kriging. The aforementioned mechanisms ensure remarkable computing performance of the modeling process and greatly improve the surrogate’s predictive power as compared to surrogates established in a full-dimensionality domain. Comparative studies carried out using three circuits and a number of recent benchmark methods corroborate the competitive performance of the introduced methodology, in particular, its ability to yield design-ready behavioral models featuring relative RMS error of a few percent at the cost corresponding to less than a few hundred of high-fidelity training points.

candidates.title: Investigation and Optimization of Air Pollution Risk by a Multi-criteria Decision Making Method Using Fuzzy TOPSIS: A Case Study of Construction Workers
candidates.abstract: Background: Investigating human health during work importantly affect the safety and efficiency of the society. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. The selection of the linear and non-linear models was conducted according to the F values, and the model parameters were estimated using the Newton-Raphson test. Most coefficients were significant at P= 0.99. The model also has a high describing value of 0.97. The final estimated homogeneity coefficient was equal to 1.31, and it ranged from 0.86 to 2.72 for the critical risk investigation. The significance of the present research is to increase the health and safety of workers during work resulting in a more sustainable and healthier environment. Conclusion: Accordingly, the managers could handle the risks, determine the tolerable risks, indicate the risk of each process to control expenses, and take the essential measures for optimization.

candidates.title: Deep reinforcement learning-driven assessment and personalized educational strategies for college students using innovation and entrepreneurship-related educational proxies
candidates.abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-Powered Diagnosis and Customized Recommendation Model of College Students’ Innovation and Entrepreneurship Achievement; new guideline to personalized education assessment and recommendation in college. Conventional assessment techniques offer below standard battery tests of the learning curve, entrepreneurial participation, behavioural change and iteration of enhancement skills of college learners within the training course of action. This research introduces an adaptive intelligent framework, the Hybrid Transformer-Graph Reinforcement Adaptive Competency Engine (HT-GRACE), to model the achievement of students’ innovation- and entrepreneurship-related educational outcomes with proxy indicators from the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD), consisting of 32,593 student records. The HT-GRACE framework integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for learning structural representations, Transformer Networks (TNs) for learning temporal behavioural representations, and Deep Reinforcement Learning using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to simulate adaptive educational policy. Students’ conditions are represented by multiple learning interaction indices, and student intervention activities, including tutoring help, participation proposals for projects, innovation collaboration proposals, and adaptive learning enrichment modules, are adopted. The awards are formalized to measure educational advancement on proxy indicators and interventions steps was interpreted as simulated or anticipated suggestions. Evaluation shows high performance, with an Accuracy of 94.8% an F1-score of 94.86% a ROC-AUC of 94.95% and an MCC of 0.915. The framework also achieves a cumulative reward gain of 27.6% and a policy divergence stability score of 0.91, demonstrating stable performance in simulated adaptive educational decision-making. Applications include intelligent academic advising, entrepreneurial preparation platforms, competency-based analytics, and AI-driven personalized higher education ecosystems for diverse learners.

candidates.title: Sequence-based artificial intelligence-guided inhibitory peptides to counteract AAV neutralizing antibodies in gene therapy.
candidates.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors have demonstrated strong clinical efficacy across multiple monogenic disorders, yet neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) remain major barriers to vector redosing and durable transduction. To address this limitation, we developed a sequence-based artificial intelligence framework integrating Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and Evolutionary Scale Modeling with Low-Rank Adaptation (ESM-LoRA) to identify human-tolerant, virus-specific motifs across human and viral proteins using sliding-window analyses and multi-layer fine-tuning. Using capsid-derived segments from AAV2 and AAV843, we prioritized surface-accessible, virus-polarized peptides as candidate decoys and evaluated their ability to block AAV-targeted antibodies. The models achieved high accuracy in distinguishing human versus viral fragments, and selected peptides bound AAV-specific antibodies with nanomolar affinity, competitively restored capsid binding, and recovered >60% of baseline transduction in the presence of NAbs. In mouse models with pre-existing or redosing-induced antibodies, coadministration of decoy peptides and an IgG-degrading enzyme reduced high-titer NAbs to approximately 1:4 and restored hepatic transgene expression without detectable inflammatory or peptide-specific immune responses. A contrastive variational autoencoder (VAE) further generated non-natural peptides with broader epitope coverage. These results support sequence-driven AI design of short, low-immunogenicity decoy peptides as a translational strategy to mitigate NAb interference and enhance the feasibility of AAV redosing.

candidates.title: Fast Solution Methods for the Classical 0–1 Knapsack Problem
candidates.abstract: The classical 0--1 knapsack problem is among the simplest integer programs to state and among the most instructive problems for understanding why algorithm selection must follow instance structure. An input contains items with positive integer weights and profits, and the task is to choose a maximum-profit subset whose total weight does not exceed a capacity. The problem is weakly NP-hard, yet many large instances are solved quickly because exact algorithms exploit moderate numeric parameters, strong linear relaxations, dominance relations, or a small set of uncertain variables near the fractional break item. This review develops a theory-guided account of the principal fast solution methods for the classical problem. It proves the correctness and complexity of weight-indexed and profit-indexed dynamic programming, explains sparse Pareto-frontier implementations and reconstruction, derives the fractional-knapsack upper bound used by branch-and-bound methods, and establishes the correctness of meet-in-the-middle search. It then presents the core concept that underlies influential practical solvers and gives a detailed proof of the standard profit-scaling fully polynomial-time approximation scheme. Modern advances based on structured min-plus convolution are placed within this classical landscape rather than treated as isolated results. The central conclusion is that there is no universally fastest knapsack algorithm. Small item counts favor meet-in-the-middle search, moderate capacities or total profits favor dynamic programming, favorable density structure favors core-based exact methods, and very large numeric coefficients favor approximation. A final decision framework translates these theoretical distinctions into an implementable solver-selection policy while identifying open questions concerning adaptivity, certified switching among methods, memory efficiency, and realistic hard-instance generation.

candidates.title: DBAASP V4: condition-resolved bioactivity and chemical structures for data-driven peptide and peptidomimetic discovery
candidates.abstract: The current peptide renaissance-driven by metagenomic and proteomic mining, molecular de-extinction, protein language models, and generative or evolutionary design-is producing millions of candidates, but useful machine learning depends on experimentally anchored, context-rich labels. The Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides (DBAASP) is a manually curated resource linking peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, and mammalian-cell cytotoxicity measurements and their experimental conditions. DBAASP v4 contains >25 000 entries and extends the resource from a sequence-centered database to a structure-aware repository. Major additions include systematic SMILES representations, enhanced annotation of intrachain bonds and ring architectures, dedicated antibiofilm, and synergy records, PubChem links, >9200 molecular-dynamics trajectories, and new prediction services. The condition-resolved data support supervised learning, strain-, and target-specific models, model calibration, and surrogate fitness functions for genetic algorithms. SMILES representations further enable modeling of noncanonical peptides and peptidomimetics that cannot be adequately described by sequence alone. DBAASP therefore complements large peptide catalogues by providing the experimentally curated activity and structure layers, needed to convert sequence information into testable predictions, design, and optimization of biologically active compounds. DBAASP v4 is freely available at https://dbaasp.org.

candidates.title: Decoding small cell lung cancer vulnerabilities: the AI pathway to next-gen therapeutics
candidates.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is aggressive, treatment-sensitive, and prone to relapse. This Review evaluates how generative AI, graph neural networks, molecular language and diffusion models, structure-based design, and multimodal learning can exploit SCLC dependencies for small-molecule discovery. candidates.title: Latent-aligned scalable interpolant transformer for controllable chest X-ray synthesis
candidates.abstract: Abstract Controllable chest X-ray (CXR) synthesis requires control over both semantic findings and their spatial relationship to thoracic anatomy. Text-conditioned generative models can specify disease labels or report-level descriptions but often provide limited control over pathology location and extent. We introduce LatAlignCXR, which represents anatomical layout, pathology location, and residual appearance within a structured latent space. Text prompts, reference radiographs, and user-defined coordinates are mapped to this representation, from which anatomical, pathology, and thoracic structural priors are decoded to condition a scalable interpolant transformer (SiT). The same representation supports text-, image-, and coordinate-conditioned synthesis. On MIMIC-CXR, LatAlignCXR achieved the highest anatomical Dice (0.6564), the lowest Fréchet distance in three of four feature spaces, and the highest pneumonia-localization consistency (Dice 0.1385, IoU 0.0741). In a blinded radiologist evaluation, LatAlignCXR received mean ratings of 4.63 for pathology consistency and 4.50 for spatial consistency, compared with 3.63 and 3.37 for Cheff, respectively. In downstream classification, synthetic augmentation increased accuracy from 69.0% to 76.0% with 1000 real images, with smaller and non-monotonic effects as real-data availability increased. These findings support structured latent conditioning for spatially controllable CXR synthesis, particularly for pathology representation and spatial consistency.

candidates.title: Contextual encoding of states and indices for episodic memories make goal-directed action selection flexible, transparent, and efficient
candidates.abstract: When we want to solve a problem, our brain helps us by recalling related experiences. Furthermore, it can selectively recall only those experiences that fit especially well to the current context and contingencies. In addition, it provides explanations for chosen actions in terms of prior experiences. We show that experimental data on underlying neural codes of the brain, in particular contextual encoding of states and index cells for episodic memories, enable us to port essential aspects of the problem solving strategy of the brain into a simple algorithm. It only requires local online learning in shallow neural networks with low resolution of synaptic weights in order to explore a new environment, and it supports low-latency decision making. Hence it is especially suited for implementation in edge devices. Surprisingly, the performance of this light-weight algorithm on a standard benchmark task, navigation in Markov Decision Processes, is competitive with that of commonly used but computationally more demanding, less flexible, and less transparent reinforcement learning approaches.

candidates.title: Simulation-based Inference with the Python Package sbijax
candidates.abstract: In natural sciences like astrophysics, biology or neuroscience, models can be frequently formulated as simulator functions, i.e., computer programs that stochastically map a parameter vector 𝜃 to synthetic data 𝑥.Even though simulators of this kind can represent realistic descriptions of real-world data-generating processes, they often emit intractable probability density functions.However, statistical inference of the parameters of a simulator requires the likelihood 𝑝(𝑥|𝜃) to be tractable, such that inference algorithms like Markov chain Monte Carlo can be applied.Simulation-based inference (SBI) circumvents this by only requiring the ability to sample from the simulator: parameters 𝜃 are drawn from the prior distribution 𝑝(𝜃), an observable 𝑥 is drawn from the simulator 𝑝(𝑥|𝜃), and the resulting pairs are used to approximate the posterior distribution.In computational statistics, neural SBI describes an emerging family of methods for Bayesian inference for simulator models that use neural networks as surrogate models.Here we introduce sbijax, a Python package that implements a wide variety of state-of-the-art methods in neural SBI using a user-friendly programming interface.Targeted at domain scientists, e.g., in computational physics or computational biology, and SBI researchers, sbijax offers a compact functional interface to construct SBI estimators and compute posterior distributions with a few lines of code.In addition, the package provides functionality for conventional approximate Bayesian computation, to compute model diagnostics, and to automatically estimate summary statistics.By virtue of being entirely written in JAX, sbijax is extremely computationally efficient, allowing rapid training of neural networks and executing code automatically in parallel on both CPU and GPU.

candidates.title: AI-Assisted Screening of Erlotinib-like Molecules for Mutant EGFR
candidates.abstract: Poster presented at the 2026 VCU VIP Showcase and Poster Symposium — 30 October 2026, Commons Ballroom, University Student Commons, Virginia Commonwealth University, Richmond, Virginia — part of Transformative Learning Week. The work is from the Vertically Integrated Project AI in Pharmaceutical Sciences: Bench to Bedside, VCU School of Pharmacy. Mutations in the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) kinase domain drive a subset of non-small cell lung cancers. The T790M “gatekeeper” mutation causes resistance to first-generation reversible inhibitors such as erlotinib by increasing the kinase’s affinity for ATP; third-generation osimertinib binds irreversibly to cysteine 797 and overcomes T790M, but the C797S mutation replaces that cysteine with serine and confers resistance. We asked whether molecules built on erlotinib’s 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold, intended as noncovalent binders, could be prioritized computationally against the T790M/C797S EGFR crystal structure 8H7X, with erlotinib as both scaffold and docking reference. Methods. A generator combined substituents at three scaffold positions (844 combinations); property filters and de-duplication left 529 molecules, ranked by Morgan-fingerprint Tanimoto similarity to erlotinib. A ring-label bug in the generator’s original text-based assembly had built all ten initially selected liberal-library structures incorrectly; the corrected builder joins molecular graphs and was cross-checked on all 844 combinations. The docking panel held erlotinib plus 29 candidates. AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 docked RDKit/Meeko-prepared ligands into one rigid 8H7X receptor and box (exhaustiveness 32; three seeds; 90 runs). Follow-up checks covered Vina score components, pose contacts, neutral and +1 charge states docked with Vina and Vinardo, and GNINA 1.3.2 rescoring. Findings. Similarity to erlotinib and docking rank were not interchangeable, and the leading candidates’ advantages changed with scoring method, pose and charge state. Twenty-six of 29 candidates scored more favorably than erlotinib under Vina, but much of the similarity trend reflected differences between library groups rather than a within-group relationship. For the three Vina leaders, fewer rotatable bonds — and so a smaller flexibility correction — outweighed weaker modeled protein-contact terms. GNINA and Vina rankings barely agreed; Vinardo erased most of the Vina leaders’ advantage; and alternative poses and charge states changed which placement looked best. In an exploratory follow-up, LibFix_07 kept a favorable mean score across the methods and states tested, but its binding orientation is unresolved. Limitations. Rigid single-ligand docking into a 3.40 Å structure cannot capture the ATP competition through which T790M acts, and all scores reported are predictions, not measured potency. Redocking the co-crystallized 8H7X ligand reproduced its pose only at the third-ranked mode, which is stated on the poster and bounds how much weight any top-ranked pose should carry. Educational context. The first four authors are undergraduate students, and they came to this problem from four different disciplines — chemistry and biochemistry, computer science, data science, and communication arts. The work is from a Vertically Integrated Project, a multi-year research team spanning academic levels, in which students use AI tools as inquiry partners under a curriculum whose central practice is verifying machine-generated claims rather than accepting them. The disciplinary mix was load-bearing rather than incidental: the errors the models did not catch were caught by different students drawing on different coursework. Catching the ring-label bug before docking, and reporting the redocking control and the scoring-function disagreements rather than the single most favorable number, are the substantive results of that practice. Analysis code, archived docking runs and checksums are held in a private team repository and are available from the corresponding author on request. Files in this record: the poster as displayed (PDF), a print-resolution PDF at final artwork size (63 × 42 in), and the editable PowerPoint source.

candidates.title: Simulating Word Suggestion Usage in Mobile Typing to Guide Intelligent Text Entry Design
candidates.abstract: Intelligent text entry (ITE) methods, such as word suggestions, are widely used in mobile typing, yet improving these systems remains challenging because the cognitive mechanisms underlying suggestion use are poorly understood and evaluating new systems often requires long-term user studies to account for behavioral adaptation. We present WSTypist, a reinforcement learning-based model that simulates how typists integrate word suggestions into typing. We extend recent hierarchical control models of typing by identifying and implementing important cognitive mechanisms that underlie high-level decision-making when integrating word suggestions into manual typing: considering orthographic processes, assessing efficiency gains, and accounting for personal preferences regarding AI support. Our evaluations show that WSTypist simulates diverse human-like suggestion-use strategies, reproduces behavioral differences, and generalizes across different systems. Through four design cases, we demonstrate how a computational rationality model can inform what-if analyses during the design process by simulating how users might adapt to changes in the UI or algorithmic support, thereby reducing the need for user studies early in the exploratory design phase.

candidates.title: Lipid Changes due to Low O-GlcNAc and the Downstream Consequences
candidates.abstract: O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) is an essential mammalian glycosyltransferase that installs O-GlcNAc onto thousands of cytosolic and nuclear proteins. Dysregulated glycosylation by OGT is associated with disease states, including cancer and neurodegeneration. However, cellular consequences of acute loss of O-GlcNAc remain poorly understood. Here, we employed a cell-permeable small molecule inhibitor of OGT, OSMI-4, coupled with transcriptomic and lipidomic analyses to characterize the effects of O-GlcNAc depletion in human cell lines. Loss of O-GlcNAc led to changes in expression of lipid metabolism genes and remodeling of the lipidome, with unsaturated phosphatidylcholines (PCs), saturated lysophosphatidylcholines (LPCs) and unsaturated storage lipids accumulating. We also observed increased lipid droplets. Our results suggest that polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) accumulate in the membrane under low O-GlcNAc conditions and that cells buffer this accumulation by removing PUFAs from membrane lipids and sequestering them in lipid droplets. We found that treatment with OSMI-4 sensitizes cells to ferroptosis inducers, likely because accumulated cell membrane PUFAs undergo peroxidation. Taken together, our results highlight lipid remodeling as an important process that mediates the downstream effects of loss of O-GlcNAc. It may be possible to exploit the synergy between OGT inhibitors and ferroptosis inducers for therapeutic benefit.

candidates.title: Reimagining antimicrobial resistance: AI-driven predictive epidemiology and the C-AMRE framework for next-generation antibiotic discovery.
candidates.abstract: Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) has evolved from a clinically observed phenomenon into a complex, dynamic, and partially predictable evolutionary process. Traditional approaches centered on phenotypic detection and retrospective surveillance are increasingly inadequate to address the accelerating pace of resistance emergence. This review presents a paradigm shift toward predictive antimicrobial science, driven by the convergence of Evolutionary Intelligence (EI), Artificial Intelligence (AI), genomic surveillance, molecular simulation, and digital twin technologies. Leveraging whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and resistome analytics, AI models can identify latent resistance determinants and forecast evolutionary trajectories before clinical manifestation, enabling a transition from reactive to anticipatory intervention strategies. Central to this transformation is the concept of the Computational Antimicrobial Resistance Ecosystem (C-AMRE), an integrated, multi-layered framework that unifies data acquisition, predictive modeling, mechanistic simulation, and clinical feedback into a continuous learning system. Within this ecosystem, molecular simulations provide mechanistic insights into resistance at atomic and systems levels, while AI-driven pharmacology enables the design of novel antibiotics, antimicrobial peptides, and Nano-Adjuvants through generative and optimization-based approaches. The incorporation of digital twins further advances precision medicine by simulating patient-specific infection dynamics, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK-PD), and resistance evolution in real time, thereby enabling adaptive and personalized therapeutic strategies. Across micro-, meso-, and macro-scales, these technologies collectively redefine AMR as a systems-level phenomenon that can be modeled, predicted, and strategically managed. However, challenges related to data integration, model interpretability, validation, ethical governance, and global accessibility remain critical barriers to implementation. Despite these limitations, the integration of AI and computational frameworks positions antimicrobial research at the forefront of a new era, where antibiotics are no longer static interventions but adaptive components of intelligent, continuously evolving systems. This review highlights the transition from detection to prediction and ultimately to adaptive intervention, emphasizing the role of computational ecosystems in shaping the future of sustainable antimicrobial therapy.

candidates.title: Metal–Organic Frameworks for Sustainable Photocatalytic and Electrocatalytic HMF‐to‐FDCA Conversion: From Catalyst Engineering to Energy‐Saving Paired Electrolysis Systems
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic and electrocatalytic upgrading of lignocellulosic biomass into value‐added chemicals offers a sustainable route to carbon neutrality. 5‑hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key intermediate because its selective oxidation yields 2,5‑furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA), a renewable monomer for biodegradable polyesters. This review summarizes metal–organic frameworks (MOFs)‐based catalysts for photo‐ and electrochemical HMF oxidation, covering pristine MOFs and MOF‐derived catalytic systems. This review further discusses key modification strategies, including dynamic structural regulation, multi‐active‐site design, and derivative structural optimization. Through these strategies, MOF‐based systems modulate electronic structure, active‐site accessibility, and mass/charge transport, thereby enhancing the activity and FDCA selectivity of photocatalytic and electrocatalytic HMF oxidation. Building on this mechanistic understanding, we examine the structure–activity relationships and reaction mechanisms revealed by in situ characterizations and density functional theory calculations. This review also assesses paired electrolysis systems that integrate anodic HMFOR with cathodic hydrogen evolution or other value‐added reductions. Finally, persistent challenges such as scalable synthesis and reactor design are addressed, along with future perspectives for rational catalyst design and industrial implementation of MOF‐based biomass upgrading.

candidates.title: Live Spatial Transcriptomics Enables Longitudinal Tissue Mapping
candidates.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has become an important technology in biomedical research by preserving the spatial context of gene expression in tissues and enabling the study of cellular states and interactions in situ. However, most existing methods provide only static snapshots of individual tissue specimens, requiring inference of the molecular dynamics underlying development, disease progression, and therapeutic response from different specimens rather than direct tracking in the same living tissue. Here, we introduce Live Spatial Transcriptomics (Live-ST), a technology that enables longitudinal, transcriptome-wide profiling of living tissue. Live-ST combines electroporation-based intracellular sampling and spatial barcoding to enable repeated, spatially resolved mRNA measurements in intact living tissue through next-generation sequencing. We demonstrate its capabilities by (i) benchmarking spatial mRNA capture in patterned two-dimensional cell systems, (ii) spatially profiling transcriptomes in intact, patient-derived living melanoma tissues while preserving tissue viability, and (iii) longitudinally tracking drug-response dynamics within the tumor microenvironment. Together, Live-ST enables repeated, non-destructive measurements of spatial gene expression, providing a new framework for studying dynamic tissue biology in native physiological and pathological contexts.

candidates.title: A Benchmarking Framework for Context-aware XR Interfaces
candidates.abstract: Everyday Extended Reality (XR) systems aim to provide context-aware access to the right functionalities at the right time and place, with minimal manual reconfiguration as users switch context. Yet these interfaces are hard to evaluate: current prototyping and user-study workflows offer no systematic, repeatable way to compare adaptation methods across users and scenarios. We present ContextXR, a novel benchmarking framework for context-aware XR interfaces. ContextXR represents an XR application as a connected graph of functional facets, each a semantically coherent group of related capabilities that together support a shared user intent.On this representation, we build MineXR++, a dataset augmenting prior XR interface data with facet-level annotations, and formulate three canonical tasks of context-aware suggestion: context factor analysis, initial facet suggestion, and next facet suggestion.Our evaluation protocol scores suggestion methods by a simulated interaction metric, the navigation and search cost of reaching the desired functionality. Through experiments benchmarking global popularity, relational retrieval, and LLM-based methods, we demonstrate that ContextXR enables the systematic, reproducible evaluation of context-aware XR interfaces.
